scope: Standalone generic Boolean matrix construction on 12,20,28,36 variables. No production solver integration, curve inputs, targets, scalar recovery, relation collection or rho campaigns.
fixtures: Each generator has 16 distinct quadratic support monomials, a constant and the first min(n,10) linear terms. Every input samples its coefficients anew and forces a quadratic term except explicit first-generator degree changes. All inputs in a batch must be distinct. Fixtures depend only on the supplied seed; no performance screening.

families_contract.quadratic: All generators remain quadratic; all variables eligible for multipliers.
families_contract.linear_drop: All variables eligible; first generator cycles quadratic, linear, quadratic, zero.
families_contract.restricted_cycle: Exactly eight evenly spaced variables eligible for multipliers; first generator cycles quadratic, linear, constant, zero.

candidate: Sparse intermediate rows with the same combinatorial ranker. Reuse one ambient scratch bitmap and marked/touched-word lists per application. Each intermediate row retains only nonzero (word index,word value) pairs; scratch and marks reset after every product even when cancellation empties a word. Build the final dense matrix only after actual-column compaction. Cold setup, sparse allocations, final dense output and validation are all charged.

controls.sorted: Port of direct sort/parity/compact constructor to u64 monomials, matching current caps.
controls.binary: Same packed rows and occupancy compaction as candidate, with binary search in the sorted ambient basis. Strong scalable lookup control.
controls.dense: Same packed constructor with a 2^n direct lookup; executed only at the n=12 bridge. Larger dimensions are NOT_EXECUTED by design, not failures or inferred times.
controls.ranked: Initial combinatorially indexed dense-intermediate constructor, freshly rerun in this binary.

correctness: Independent recursive multiplier enumeration, set parity and column-major incidence oracle. Exhaustive rank agreement with numeric enumeration through n=12; independent combination enumeration at n=20/28/36. All 6144 n=3 coefficient/degree/active-mask cases checked across all constructors, plus context changes, invalid inputs, current caps and a full-width constant-generator resource refusal. Sparse arm joins all exhaustive and larger fixture checks; an eighth test exercises word cancellation/reactivation, scratch reset between rows and full-support compaction.
accounting: Cold setup, every application, intermediate and final allocation, support compaction, exact validation and destruction. Fixtures/oracles are common supplied-input costs outside arm timings, inside process receipts. Twenty repetitions rotate four arms, or five at the bridge. All raw samples retained.
memory: Retained Rust structure and Vec capacities, excluding allocator metadata. Separate output payload, total rows/columns and lookup-entry count. Fresh-worker peak RSS includes all variants and reference matrices and is not candidate-specific. Ranked removes only the exponential lookup, not the ambient degree<=D basis or dense-row footprint.
performance_gate: At n=20,28,36, batch32, every family: sparse_rank must have a 95 percent paired-bootstrap lower bound above 2.0 against sorted, and above 1.05 against both binary and ranked. All 27 gates required; bridge at n=12 reported separately. No post-holdout tuning.
classification: Finite generic construction engineering diagnostic. Full solver time, operation calibration, end-to-end IC cost and rho ratio remain null. Goal of dramatic complete-algorithm improvement is not proven by this stage experiment.
predecessor: run_01 is retained unchanged: rank indexing removed the exponential lookup but the 18-gate dramatic scaling requirement failed. run_02 tests sparse intermediates on new holdouts with fresh same-binary controls.
